identity.trade: Flour and bread: the great windmill grinds the vale's wheat; the bakehouse feeds three villages.

greeting: Bring me a problem with a name and a number. Then we can talk.
First time in Millbrook? The Millbrook Great Mill is the place to start.
rumour: Strangers stop here more than they used to. Not all of them buy anything.
A well on the east road runs dry every dusk and fills by dawn. Nobody wants to ask why.
A sack of Millbrook flour is said to be good luck on a stoneless road.

opinions.orrin_dobbin: Orrin lives next door and hears everything I do.
opinions.osric_dalby: I would trust Osric with a purse. A small one.

time.morning: Early start. The field has been awake an hour.

dialogue.aside: A friend is a rare coin. I have spent worse.

greeting: Ale is fair, stew is hot, and I do not do credit.
Strangers in Millbrook get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: Harvest crews drink the barley they cut. Somebody should tax that circle.
Travellers say the stones are dimmer on the east road. I water the ale, not the news.
The scarecrow by the north field has moved twice. The farmer says he did not touch it.
Thornfield's brewer pays for barley in ale. The miller prefers that.

opinions.hilde_harrow: Hilde keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.evening: Last light. The work is done or it is dark. Both are fine.

dialogue.aside: Mind the order of things, friend. There. Now we can talk.

greeting: Quick job or good job? I charge for both.
Harvest is the only holiday we keep. The rest is work.
rumour: Plough blades, sickles, hinges. Honest iron for honest mud.
The forge hums when the stones dim. Not loud. Enough to notice.
Barn cats bring in too many rats and too few mice. Odd, that.

opinions.hilde_harrow: Hilde is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.night: Shouldn't you be inside? The fields are quiet, but the dark has ears.

greeting: Take your time. Touch nothing you cannot afford.
Fields do not wait for visitors, but I will spare a moment.
rumour: Seed, rope and lamp oil. The three things every farmer remembers on the last day.
Candles are short this month. The wax comes late, and so does the honest news.
A cart of seed went missing between the barn and the mill. No tracks.
Folk say Millbrook was founded by someone who wanted to be left alone. We have not forgotten.

opinions.dalla_thackeray: Dalla undercuts me. I forgive Dalla. Mostly.

time.rain: Rain. Good for the barley, bad for the knees. Bless it.

dialogue.aside: Welcome. Wipe your boots. Please. Soap is dear and floors are dearer.

greeting: Mind the flour. It gets everywhere, opinions included.
Millbrook is mill and bakehouse. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: The oven runs hot because the town runs hungry.
The hedgerows grow faster than the hedger can trim. I trimmed twice this month.
The mill sails turned backward on their own last Tuesday. Flour everywhere.

opinions.leofric_woolcott: Leofric undercuts me. I forgive Leofric. Mostly.
opinions.odell_tyndall: Odell keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.morning: Early start. The field has been awake an hour.

dialogue.aside: Forgive me. It has been a long week and a longer day. Still, it is good to see you.

greeting: You are somebody's grandchild. I can tell by the walk.
Folk come to Millbrook for mill and bakehouse. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: When I was young the stones sang at dusk. Now they hum, like someone ill.
Wolves keep to the hedge line and never cross it. As if the hedge were a wall.

opinions.dalla_thackeray: Dalla lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.evening: Last light. The work is done or it is dark. Both are fine.

dialogue.aside: You look rough. Eat something. That is not advice, it is an order.

greeting: Grain is weight, flour is weight, patience is the one thing I cannot sell.
Good boots. The fields are that way.
rumour: The mice left the mill. All of them, in one night. That is not a good sign.
The old well tastes of iron this season. I do not say the stones are why.

opinions.freya_brook: Freya keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.
opinions.yarrow_lovell: Yarrow works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Shouldn't you be inside? The fields are quiet, but the dark has ears.

dialogue.aside: Excuse the dust. Work does not stop for friends, though it does pause.

greeting: Wheat is gold, rats are thieves, I am the law.
Millbrook is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: The count is off by a sack. One sack. It is always one sack.
The wheat came up thin on the stone side and thick on the far side. Odd.
Ask in Millbrook who built the Millbrook Great Mill and you will get a different name each time.

opinions.gethin_fletcher: Gethin works hard and talks harder.
opinions.hadley_wythe: Hadley keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.rain: Rain. Good for the barley, bad for the knees. Bless it.

dialogue.aside: Excuse the dust. Work does not stop for friends, though it does pause.

greeting: Soil does not care who you are. It cares what you do on Tuesdays.
You will hear Millbrook before you see it. Ask at the Millbrook Great Mill.
rumour: Crows are thick this year. They knew about the harvest before I did.
Crows gather on the east field in a ring. Not feeding. Standing.

opinions.hadley_wythe: Hadley works hard and talks harder.
opinions.isolt_charnock: Isolt knows the trade. I will say that for Isolt.

time.morning: Early start. The field has been awake an hour.

dialogue.aside: Take your time, friend. I am in no hurry. I am, in fact, very good at waiting.

greeting: Rain tomorrow. My knee says so.
Welcome to Millbrook. Mind the Millbrook Great Mill. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: Violet at the field edge, only a little. I am told it is the light.
The reeve's tally says forty sacks. The barn says thirty-eight. The barn is honest.
When Millbrook is quiet we say it is peaceful. When it is very quiet we say nothing.

opinions.hadley_wythe: Hadley knows the trade. I will say that for Hadley.

time.evening: Last light. The work is done or it is dark. Both are fine.

dialogue.aside: A bright day and a bright friend! What luck!

greeting: Grain in, flour out. Everything else is chatter.
The Millbrook Great Mill is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: Flour weighs light lately. The scales are honest. I checked.
The Millbrook Great Mill drew a stranger last month. He asked questions and bought nothing.

opinions.brannoc_blackmore: Brannoc knows the trade. I will say that for Brannoc.
opinions.gavin_swale: Gavin works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Shouldn't you be inside? The fields are quiet, but the dark has ears.

dialogue.aside: I dreamed of you last night. You were a heron. It suited you.

greeting: Hold the mule. He is not as bad as he looks.
rumour: Toll keepers keep changing. Their prices are the only thing that stays the same.
If trade slows, Millbrook feels it first. If it speeds up, Millbrook feels it last.

opinions.elka_sparrow: Elka and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.
opinions.gethin_fletcher: Gethin works hard and talks harder.

time.rain: Rain. Good for the barley, bad for the knees. Bless it.

dialogue.aside: My friend. Come, I kept something for you. A small thing. It means a lot to me.

greeting: Do not stand between a ewe and her lamb. She will not read the sign.
rumour: Counted forty, home came thirty-nine. The dog looks guilty.
The Millbrook Great Mill was busy last week. Something is stirring, or somebody is.

opinions.brannoc_blackmore: Brannoc keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.
opinions.isolt_charnock: Isolt works hard and talks harder.

time.morning: Early start. The field has been awake an hour.

dialogue.aside: Up before dawn, friend? Then you saw the best of the day. I saw it first.

greeting: Quiet work, wood. I like the quiet.
rumour: Found an axe head grown into a trunk, old as my grandmother. Nobody here owns it.
Every few years Millbrook has a winter nobody forgets. The old folk say this one is early.

opinions.gavin_swale: Gavin lives next door and hears everything I do.
opinions.isolt_charnock: Isolt knows the trade. I will say that for Isolt.

time.evening: Last light. The work is done or it is dark. Both are fine.

dialogue.aside: You have a new scar, and fewer coins than last time. Sit.

greeting: Mud is honest. Walk on it.
rumour: Seed is dear and wheat is cheap. Somebody is laughing and it is not me.
The Millbrook Great Mill has seen odder days than this. Nobody remembers when.

opinions.freya_brook: Freya knows the trade. I will say that for Freya.
opinions.isolt_charnock: Isolt works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Shouldn't you be inside? The fields are quiet, but the dark has ears.

dialogue.aside: Excuse the dust. Work does not stop for friends, though it does pause.

greeting: I am not lost. I am exploring.
rumour: I saw a light in the hedge last night. Do not tell Mum.
The scarecrow by the north field has moved twice. The farmer says he did not touch it.

opinions.norah_sparrow: Norah is blood. That settles most arguments and starts the rest.

clues.note: A sack by the door has been slit and sewn back up. It is lighter than it should be.
Boot prints, one heel worn down, coming and going. They stop where the lane meets the mill yard.
Someone re-inked a line of the count. The ink is newer than the page.
Prints too big for a dog, heading for the tree line.
A dragged carcass. Teeth marks, not knife marks.
A rail splintered outward, wool snagged on the edge.

stashes.say: You shoulder four sacks of wheat from the bin.
You pick three clean bundles of the healer's herbs.
